verificationPolicy: Primary and authoritative sources are preferred. Copyrighted PMI standards are summarized and cited, not reproduced. Time-sensitive facts must be reverified before public release.

sources.title: Project Management Professional (PMP) Examination Content Outline, July 2026
keyFacts: The examination domains are People 33 percent, Process 41 percent, and Business Environment 26 percent.
Approximately 40 percent of items represent predictive approaches and approximately 60 percent are divided between adaptive or agile and hybrid approaches.
The examination is scenario based and requires candidates to apply project management concepts and experience to realistic work situations.
The outline includes 8 People tasks, 10 Process tasks, and 8 Business Environment tasks.
sources.usageLimitations: Public outline may be summarized and briefly quoted with attribution. No confidential examination items, exam forms, or proprietary PMI courseware may be reproduced.

sources.title: Project Management Professional (PMP) Certification
sources.sourceType: Official certification requirements and exam information
keyFacts: The examination contains 180 questions.
The examination time is 240 minutes.
Candidates need 35 hours of Project Professional training unless an accepted alternative applies.
Experience requirements vary by educational pathway and must be accrued within the current eligibility window.
sources.usageLimitations: Requirements can change. Learners must verify current eligibility directly with PMI before applying.

sources.title: What Is New in the Updated PMP Exam
keyFacts: The July 2026 exam adds greater emphasis on AI, sustainability, stakeholder engagement, value, outcomes, and business impact.
PMI announced planned late Q4 2026 changes affecting eligibility of live training providers.
PMI states that self-paced courses may be taken from any organization under the announced training model, while learners remain responsible for confirming current rules.
sources.usageLimitations: Training-provider rules are time sensitive and must be checked before marketing or issuing training-hour records.

sources.title: A Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK Guide), Eighth Edition and The Standard for Project Management
keyFacts: The eighth edition emphasizes value delivery, adaptability, accountability, AI, procurement, and sustainability.
PMI describes six core principles and seven performance domains.
The guide is a professional standard and reference, while the examination outline defines what the certification exam tests.
sources.usageLimitations: Copyrighted content must be paraphrased or used under license. Substantial excerpts, figures, process tables, and proprietary teaching content require PMI permission.

sources.owner: Project Management Institute and Agile Alliance
sources.title: Agile Practice Guide, Second Edition
keyFacts: The guide is framework neutral and addresses agile practice across projects, products, portfolios, and enterprise initiatives.
The current edition includes distributed work, AI-enabled delivery, sustainability, psychological safety, scaling, and measurable value.
It supports selection of fit-for-purpose predictive, agile, and hybrid approaches.
sources.usageLimitations: Copyrighted content must be summarized and cited. Obserra exercises and questions must be original.

sources.title: Process Groups: A Practice Guide
keyFacts: The guide presents initiating, planning, executing, monitoring and controlling, and closing for primarily predictive work.
It describes 49 project management processes as commonly useful practices rather than universal prescriptions.
sources.usageLimitations: Do not reproduce proprietary process tables, detailed inputs, tools, techniques, outputs, or licensed graphics without permission.

sources.title: PMI Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct and Ethics Guidelines
sources.jurisdiction: PMI members, volunteers, certification holders, and applicants
keyFacts: PMI identifies responsibility, respect, fairness, and honesty as the values driving ethical conduct.
Certification applicants and holders are within the stated scope of the code.
sources.usageLimitations: Use short attributed excerpts only when necessary. Learners should consult the current official code for controlling language.

sources.title: GAO Schedule Assessment Guide: Best Practices for Project Schedules
sources.jurisdiction: United States federal oversight guidance with broader project applicability
keyFacts: GAO presents ten best practices for developing and maintaining a reliable, high-quality integrated schedule.
An integrated schedule models time, dependencies, milestones, critical path, resources, and the effects of change.
A credible schedule can provide early warning that a program may require corrective action.
sources.usageLimitations: Government publication may be quoted with attribution, but course visuals and examples should remain original unless rights are confirmed.

sources.title: Cost Estimating and Assessment Guide: Best Practices for Developing and Managing Program Costs
sources.jurisdiction: United States federal oversight guidance with broader project applicability
keyFacts: Reliable cost estimates support planning, budgeting, management, and oversight.
The guide addresses technical baselines, work breakdown structures, assumptions, data, methods, sensitivity, risk analysis, documentation, and updates using actual costs.
GAO associates reliable estimates with comprehensive, well-documented, accurate, and credible characteristics.
sources.usageLimitations: Government publication may be quoted with attribution. Application to private-sector projects should be presented as transferable practice, not a legal requirement.

sources.title: Healthcare.gov: CMS Has Taken Steps to Address Problems, but Needs to Further Implement Systems Development Best Practices
sources.jurisdiction: United States federal information technology oversight
keyFacts: GAO reported ineffective project oversight associated with an unreliable schedule, incomplete estimates of remaining work, outdated documentation, and inconsistent progress reviews.
The program later improved requirements management and test documentation, while additional weaknesses remained.
sources.usageLimitations: Use the case to analyze documented management conditions. Do not claim a single cause or that one method would have guaranteed success.

sources.title: James Webb Space Telescope: Technical Challenges Have Caused Schedule Strain and May Increase Costs
sources.jurisdiction: United States federal aerospace acquisition oversight
keyFacts: At the time of the report, GAO stated that project costs had increased 95 percent and launch was delayed more than 6.5 years from the 2009 baseline.
Integration and testing challenges created schedule pressure and led to additional cost and schedule analysis.
NASA expanded oversight and addressed recommendations from an independent review board.
sources.usageLimitations: Facts describe the project at the report date and must not be presented as current status. Avoid hindsight bias and single-cause conclusions.

sources.title: NASA: Assessments of Major Projects
sources.jurisdiction: United States federal aerospace acquisition oversight
keyFacts: For fiscal year 2025, NASA planned about 74 billion dollars in major-project investment.
GAO reported that four of 18 projects had cost overruns and three had schedule delays during the assessment period.
GAO stated that three of 53 historically analyzed projects accounted for almost half of total overruns.
sources.usageLimitations: Portfolio statistics are dated to the fiscal year 2025 assessment and are not general failure rates for all projects.
